title: Isaiah 42
paragraphs: ¹ 'Here is my servant, whom I uphold — my chosen one, in whom my soul delights. I have placed my Spirit upon him; he will bring justice to the nations. ² He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets. ³ A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out; faithfully he will bring forth justice. ⁴ He will not falter or be discouraged until he establishes justice on earth; the coastlands wait for his instruction.' ⁵ This is what God, the LORD, says — the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and all that comes from it, who gives breath to its people and life to those who walk on it:

⁶ 'I, the LORD, have called you for a righteous purpose; I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations — ⁷ to open blind eyes, to bring captives out of prison, and to release from the dungeon those who sit in darkness. ⁸ I am the LORD; that is my name! I will not yield my glory to another or my praise to carved idols. ⁹ The former things have come to pass, and I now declare new things; before they spring up I announce them to you.' ¹⁰ Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise from the ends of the earth — you who go down to the sea, and all that fills it, you coastlands and all who dwell in them.

¹¹ Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, and the villages where Kedar dwells; let the inhabitants of Sela sing for joy, let them shout from the mountaintops. ¹² Let them give glory to the LORD and proclaim his praise in the coastlands. ¹³ The LORD will march out like a warrior; he will rouse his zeal like a soldier in battle. He will shout, yes, roar aloud; he will triumph over his enemies. ¹⁴ For a long time I have kept silent; I have held back and restrained myself. But now I will cry out like a woman in labor, gasping and panting. ¹⁵ I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation; I will turn rivers into dry land and dry up the pools.

¹⁶ I will lead the blind along an unfamiliar path; I will guide them along ways they have not known. I will make darkness into light before them and turn the rough places smooth. These are the things I will do; I will not abandon them. ¹⁷ But those who trust in idols and say to cast images, 'You are our gods' — they will be turned back and utterly disgraced. ¹⁸ Listen, you who are deaf! Look, you who are blind, and see! ¹⁹ Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one devoted to me, blind like the LORD's servant? ²⁰ You have seen much but taken nothing in; your ears are open but you do not hear.

²¹ It pleased the LORD for the sake of his righteousness to make his law great and glorious. ²² But this is a people plundered and looted, all of them trapped in pits or hidden away in prisons. They have been plundered with no one to rescue them, and despoiled with no one to say, 'Give them back.' ²³ Who among you will listen to this? Who will pay attention and take heed for the future? ²⁴ Who gave Jacob over to be plundered, and Israel to be looted? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They refused to walk in his ways and would not obey his law. ²⁵ So he poured out on them his burning anger and the violence of war; it blazed up around them, but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they took no notice.
